questions.question: How are events related to the sample space?
options: Events are numbers outside the sample space
Events replace the sample space once probabilities are assigned
Events must contain every outcome in the sample space
Events are subsets of the sample space

questions.question: If $S=\{HH,HT,TH,TT\}$ for two coin tosses, which object is an outcome in $S$?
options: $HT$
$S^c$
$P(HH)$

questions.question: In a chosen model of a random experiment, what is the sample space $S$?
options: The set of all outcomes that the model allows
The one outcome that occurs in a particular run
The set of outcomes that have positive probability
The rule that assigns a probability to each event

questions.question: A red die and a blue die, each with faces $1$ to $6$, are rolled, and the model records the pair (red face, blue face). Which set is the sample space?
options: $\{(i,j)\colon i,j\in\{1,\ldots,6\}\}$
$\{(i,j)\colon 1\le i\le j\le 6\}$
$\{(i,j)\colon i,j\in\{1,\ldots,6\},\ i+j=7\}$

questions.question: A coin is tossed repeatedly until the first head appears, and the number of tosses is recorded. Which set is the sample space?
Two coin tosses have outcomes $HH,HT,TH,TT$. A coarser model records only the number of heads, with sample space $\{0,1,2\}$. Which event can still be expressed in the coarser model?
options: The first toss is heads
The second toss is heads
Exactly one toss is heads
The first toss is heads and the second is tails

questions.question: Two fair coins are tossed. Compare the sample spaces $S_1=\{HH,HT,TH,TT\}$ and $S_2=\{0,1,2\}$ (number of heads). Which statement is correct?
options: Both are valid, but only the outcomes of $S_1$ are equally likely
Only $S_1$ is valid, because sample space outcomes must be equally likely
Both are valid, and in $S_2$ each count has probability $\tfrac13$
Only $S_2$ is valid, because $HT$ and $TH$ are the same result

questions.question: One die with faces $1$ to $6$ is rolled. Each set below is proposed as a sample space recording some aspect of the roll. Which one is not a valid sample space?
options: $\{\text{odd},\ \text{even}\}$
$\{\text{at most }3,\ \text{at least }4\}$

questions.question: A die with faces $1$ to $6$ is rolled, and the result is to be recorded as one element of the set $S=\{\text{at most }3,\ \text{at least }3\}$. Why is this $S$ not a valid sample space for the roll?
options: A roll of $3$ fits both elements, while each roll must give exactly one
A sample space must list the six faces themselves, not categories
Its two elements do not have the same probability of occurring
An outcome must be a number, not a description such as at most $3$
